name: suite-query-failure-reconciliation
body:
Defect + reconciliation [verified against this branch's code graph and source; the brief's FQNs were the MAIN-checkout ones, corrected below].

Defect: opencode suite tools that shell out to `apg query` and parse its CSV output feed runCypher's error string straight into csvToRows. `runCypher` (opencode-suite/lib/apg.ts:54-68) returns `"Error: no apg/.trans/db.lbug found …"` or `"apg query failed (exit N):\n<message>"` on failure; `csvToRows` (apg.ts:132-139) is line-based, so the error parses as rows. `apg_plan_tasks` (opencode-suite/tools/apg_plan_tasks.ts:25-37) destructures the rows and calls `fqn.replace(...)` on an undefined `fqn` → `undefined is not an object (evaluating 'fqn.replace')`, masking the real `apg query failed` cause. Observed live by a reviewer whose apg_plan_tasks call hit a transient DB-lock error.

Dead-code guard: `isQueryError` (apg.ts:145-147) and `expectQueryOk` (apg.ts:155-158) already implement exactly this guard — expectQueryOk's doc comment names the identical prior crash `'body.replace'` — but NO tool imports them. Verified twice: a grep over opencode-suite finds only the definitions, and the code graph shows `expectQueryOk` has no callers (it is called by nothing; `isQueryError` is called only by `expectQueryOk`). The guard is dead code, so the class recurred.

Blast radius (source-verified, because the code graph does NOT resolve the cross-file tool→lib calls — the tools' anonymous `execute` arrows are not Function nodes, so `csvToRows` shows 0 callers and `runCypher` only its in-file callers): 3 tools parse CSV (`apg_plan_tasks`, `apg_plan`, `apg_plan_phases`); 14 more call runCypher and return/echo its output directly (a failure surfaces as raw error text, not a crash — inconsistent but not fatal).

What changed:
- Added `requirements.requirement.suite-tools-surface-query-failures` (feature `agent-refinement`), contained by `requirements.requirement.agent-refinement`.
- Domain realisation narrowed: the requirement now drives `domain.service.suite-query-execution` (contained by `domain.group.agent-suite`), which is realised only by `solution.component.suite-tool-wrappers`. Driving the broad `domain.group.agent-suite` reached BOTH the whole-suite `solution.system.agent-suite` and the component, and both anchored to `apg.main` — a Rust dispatcher no task genuinely changes — forcing a phantom `modifies apg.main` coverage task. The narrower service leaves `solution.system.agent-suite` unreachable from this requirement, so it is coverage-exempt here (it remains a legitimate delivery anchor for other requirements and keeps its own `apg.main` edge).
- Re-anchored the component: `implemented-by apg-opencode-suite.lib.apg.csvToRows` (was the stale `apg.main`). The FQN is stable because `opencode-suite/package.json` now declares the npm `name` `apg-opencode-suite` (commit 42fbbaa7), making the TS module identity manifest-declared and checkout-independent.
- Recorded the underlying law as `global.constraint.checkout-independent-module-identity`. The frontend fallback itself (deriving an unnamed package's identity from the directory basename) is NOT yet fixed — only instance-fixed by naming this one package — and ships as a target-less plan task.

Contradictions found vs the brief:
1. The brief's FQNs (`apg.opencode-suite.lib.apg.runCypher`) were the MAIN-checkout FQNs; on this branch the TS module prefix was the checkout directory basename (`suite-query-error-guard.`). Resolved by naming the manifest: the FQNs are now the stable `apg-opencode-suite.*` in every checkout, so they ARE anchorable. The new domain narrowing + re-anchor supersedes the earlier "keeps its stable `implemented-by apg.main` embedding anchor" rationale.
2. The graph does not resolve the tool→lib Calls (see blast radius) — the crash sites are source facts, not graph facts; only `runCypher`/`csvToRows`/`isQueryError`/`expectQueryOk` resolve as scanned Functions in `opencode-suite/lib/apg.ts`.
3. The crash is confirmed in `apg_plan_tasks` (destructured `fqn` undefined). `apg_plan` and `apg_plan_phases` mis-parse the error into garbage and can hide the cause, but do not show the same `undefined.replace` crash on the destructured `fqn`.

Coverage note for the plan-writer: the reached solution path is now `requirement → domain.service.suite-query-execution → solution.component.suite-tool-wrappers → implemented-by apg-opencode-suite.lib.apg.csvToRows`. Task-1 (`modifies apg-opencode-suite.lib.apg.csvToRows`) satisfies that coverage; the phantom delivery-anchor task against `apg.main` is no longer needed for this requirement and can be dropped.
